quotes.quote: Stand up and grip the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing towards you) about shoulder width apart, then sit down.
Grab the bar a little bit closer than shoulder-width apart with your palms facing you. You can choose to wrap your thumb around the bar or use a thumbless grip.
That’s likely because it’s less strain on your shoulders for your forearms to be supinated (palms facing you) when they’re closer together.
Sit down on the lat pulldown machine and adjust the pads so they sit tightly against your thighs.
Lean back slightly (no more than a 30 degree angle), using your legs to support your body (low back).
Avoid any additional backwards lean during the pull movement.
Lower the bar towards your chest by pulling your elbows back and down towards the glutes, stopping when the bar passes just below chin height.
It’s important to avoid using momentum to pull the bar down so that the correct muscles are engaged. Think about keeping your torso stable
Pulling the bar further down forces your forearms and deltoids to take over, shifting the load away from your lats and biceps.
Reverse the movement by slowly extending the arms, allowing the cable to pull the bar back up with control.
If you don’t have any control of the bar when it rises back to the top position, you’re likely lifting too heavy.
initiate the downward pull by first depressing (lower) your scapulae
Continue pulling until the bar nears or touches your chest, or more importantly, you observe your elbows no longer moving downward, but now beginning to move backwards.
Avoid any further pulling as this places additiomnal stresses into the shoulder joint.
